title: Unprotected concurrent access across sibling Tasks
description: Shared `counter` is written/accessed from sibling Task timelines without a modeled sync edge. dual_timeline; shared=`counter`; timeline_a=Task@14→write@15; timeline_b=Task@17→write@18; sync_gap=no await/join between sibling Tasks
risk: Concurrent mutation of shared state can race. Confirm with Swift concurrency tooling; this finding is a dual-timeline witness for one narrow pattern, not a global race proof.
path_summary: dual_timeline; shared=`counter`; timeline_a=Task@14→write@15; timeline_b=Task@17→write@18; sync_gap=no await/join between sibling Tasks

proof.trigger_condition: Call `spawnRace` so sibling Tasks touch shared `counter` without a join.
proof.expected_behavior: Dual-timeline witness for unprotected concurrent access. Pattern-scoped; not a global race proof.
assumptions: Sibling Task / Task.detached hops only; TaskGroup and actor hops excluded.
Await after the last Task hop suppresses this witness (conservative join).
Does not claim races outside this narrow pattern.
proof.content:
Timeline A (`task:expr:fixtures/swift/vertical/sibling_task_shared_race.swift:call:14:5:5`):
  - Task hop at L14
  - call `bumpA` writes `counter` at L15
Timeline B (`task:expr:fixtures/swift/vertical/sibling_task_shared_race.swift:call:17:5:10`):
  - Task hop at L17
  - call `bumpB` writes `counter` at L18
Sync gap: no await/join between sibling Tasks
This is a pattern-scoped dual-timeline race witness for sibling Tasks only. It does not prove global race freedom.

recommended_fix: Isolate the mutable state in an actor, protect it with synchronization, or await/join Tasks before overlapping access.
